correctness.rationale: For the independent-clock process used in the proof, immediately after A activates the opinion pair (u,v) represents (u,u,v). Conditional Poisson evolution over length t gives expectations u+(v−u)te^(−t) at B and u+(v−u)e^(−t) at C. Averaging gives the stated 2-by-2 stochastic matrix and invariant row ((1−φ)/K,m/K). For each indicator opinion, that row gives a bounded martingale. At every later renewal the conditional chance that C activates before B and before the next renewal is (1−E[e^(−2T)])/2>0; this ensures almost-sure absorption and justifies using the martingale to read fixation probabilities. The first interval U gives coefficients p_B=(1−φ)E[e^(−U)]/K and p_C=((1−φ)E[Ue^(−U)]+mE[e^(−U)])/K. For the equilibrium residual the two transforms are 1−φ and 1−φ−m (differentiate (1−E[e^(−sT)])/s at 1); substituting establishes equality of p_B and p_C. Erlang-2 gives K=23/27 and checks the two vectors and strict inequalities 25/69>23/69>19/69. This argument needs independence of A's renewals and the Poisson clocks, as used in the frozen renewal/memorylessness argument; marginal clock laws alone do not suffice.
